summary: One check fails: the claimed full-hold parachute speed (3.99 m/s) is 21% off what the stated canopy actually flew (4.83 m/s), because the claim is computed on a 1,504 kg ship and the simulator flew 2,205 kg — and the deeper problem behind it, that the harness's hold is 42% lighter than the catalog's own shipping slice, is flagged for the human because no agent's artifact can fix it.

checks.statement: There is exactly one band, every catalog piece sits inside it, and only bottom/middle/top sample keys appear in the params.
checks.evidence: bands has one entry, 50,000-280,000 m. Catalog altitudes run 52,500 (torn_foil_blanket) to 277,000 (armstrongs_module); all 30 pieces fall inside, min margin 2,500 m at the floor and 3,000 m at the ceiling. Sample-keyed params objects are ablation.heat_index, ablation.cost_curve and ablation.optimal_skims, each with exactly the keys bottom/middle/top and no others.

checks.statement: Every band_summary entry agrees with the debris array it summarises: piece_count, mean_mass_kg and fragile_fraction recomputed.
checks.evidence: Thirds of the 230,000 m envelope split at 126,667 and 203,333 m. Bottom: 11 pieces (52,500-120,000), masses sum 1,985 -> 1985/11 = 180.45 (claimed 180.45); fragile spawn weight 3+2+2+2 = 9 over total 89 = 0.1011 (claimed 0.1011). Middle: 10 pieces (131,000-197,500), sum 3,671 -> 367.10 (claimed 367.1); fragile 3+4+3+2 = 12 over 69 = 0.17391 (claimed 0.1739). Top: 9 pieces (209,000-277,000), sum 7,705 -> 856.11 (claimed 856.11); fragile 3+2+3+2 = 10 over 40 = 0.2500 (claimed 0.25). All nine figures match.

checks.statement: The catalog's mean piece mass rises with altitude, third over third.
checks.evidence: 180.45 -> 367.10 -> 856.11 kg, monotone, 2.03x then 2.33x, 4.74x end to end. Excluding armstrongs_module the top third still reads 4,105/8 = 513.13 kg, so the rise is not an artefact of the fixed objective: 180.45 -> 367.10 -> 513.13, 2.84x end to end.

checks.statement: Fragile spawn share rises with altitude, roughly 1 in 10 at the bottom to 1 in 4 at the top.
checks.evidence: Spawn-weighted: 9/89 = 0.1011 (1 in 9.9), 12/69 = 0.1739 (1 in 5.8), 10/40 = 0.2500 (1 in 4.0). Monotone and lands on both stated endpoints. Counted by piece instead it would read 4/11, 4/10, 4/9 — nearly flat — so the weighted figure is the one that carries the design intent.

checks.statement: A full hold roughly doubles the rocket's mass at starting storage size.
checks.evidence: shipping_slice.slots_per_piece is 1, so six base slots carry six pieces. Representative piece = spawn-weighted mean over the hand-tetherable slice (bottom two thirds, 19 pieces): mass-weight 13,416 (bottom, weight 87) + 22,295 (middle, weight 67) = 35,711 over weight 154 = 231.89 kg. 6 x 231.89 = 1,391.3 kg against dry_mass_kg 1,400 -> all-up 2,791.3, ratio 1.994x, 0.3% off doubling, and within 0.5% of GDD 2.2's own flown full hold of ~1,398 kg. Recorded for the human: the simulator's own hold model disagrees with both — cargo.kg_per_slot 134.25, full_hold_kg 805.5, full_hold_mass_ratio 1.58 — which is 42% light against the catalog. That gap is an instrument disagreement, not a value either owner can move, and it is carried into observations because it makes several flown figures optimistic.

checks.statement: Each cost_curve minimum equals the matching optimal_skims entry, and the curve is what the stated ablation model actually produces.
checks.evidence: Model from balance_notes and params.ablation: cost(s,k) = SUM(i=0..k) 3.1*1.17^i + 0.0009*(heat_index[s]*mult[k])^2 + k*0.0009*46.7^2. Cumulative tolls 3.100/6.727/10.971/15.936; per-skim term 0.0009*2,180.89 = 1.963. Bottom entry terms 0.0009*100^2 = 9.000 (k=0) and 0.0009*43.40^2 = 1.695 (k>=1): k=0 -> 12.100 (array 12.10), k=1 -> 10.385 (10.39), k=2 -> 16.591 (16.59), k=3 -> 23.519 (23.52). Middle 0.0009*125^2 = 14.063 and 0.0009*54.25^2 = 2.649: 17.163/11.339/17.545/24.473 against 17.16/11.34/17.54/24.47. Top 0.0009*160^2 = 23.040 and 0.0009*69.44^2 = 4.340: 26.140/13.029/19.236/26.164 against 26.14/13.03/19.24/26.16. Every one of the twelve points reproduces to better than 0.1%. Argmins are k=1 at all three samples, matching optimal_skims {bottom 1, middle 1, top 1}. balance_notes states this exact model, not a different one. Judged only on the curve, the model and the skim study; the pass-count tables were not used.

checks.statement: The endgame haul cannot plunge home from the top of the band at any legal entry depth, a survivable multi-pass route exists for it, and an empty ship and a full hold can still plunge from anywhere in the band.
checks.evidence: Floor first: reentry.commit_floor_m 8,000 against atmosphere_top_m 43,000 — 35,000 m below the interface, so it constrains rather than decorates. Judged on committed_descents only. (1) Endgame haul, top of band: plunge_peak_heat 265.3 with the entry pinned at the floor, against the highest shield tier the shop sells, heat_capacity 245 — 8.3% over, so no purchase buys the plunge back (GDD 2.2's ceiling rule, stated there as 268.8; flown 265.3). (2) A survivable multi-pass route exists: the same row gives 203.4 at one skim and 188.9 at two, both under 215 (heat_shield tier 1) and under 245 (tier 2), so the finale flies with a shield purchase and one or two braking passes — GDD 2.6's 'reachable and landable only near full upgrades' in bar units. Base capacity 185 forbids it, which is the intended gate, not a failure. (3) At base capacity 185, one pass from anywhere: empty 93.2/114.2/144.7 (bottom/middle/top), full hold 117.6/143.0/180.1, half hold 106.1/129.5/163.5 — every one under 185, so aerobraking stays special rather than mandatory. Margin at the binding case is thin (180.1 vs 185 = 2.7%; the heaviest ordinary piece at 828 kg reads 181.0, 2.2%) and the flown full hold was 805.5 kg rather than the catalog's 1,391 kg — both carried to observations.

checks.statement: The claimed skim_heat_multiplier matches the measured array for the top sample, entry by entry, within 0.10.
checks.evidence: params.ablation.skim_heat_multiplier [1.000, 0.434, 0.434, 0.434] against skims.top.skim_heat_multiplier_measured [1.000, 0.434, 0.434, 0.434]. Deltas 0.000/0.000/0.000/0.000 at indices 0-3, tolerance 0.10. The top study was flown at entry depth 0 m with the skim altitude scanned to 23,650 m, and heat_index.top 160 matches skims.top entry_peak_heat 160.0 exactly, so multiplier and index share one basis and their product is meaningful.

checks.statement: skim_heat_multiplier starts at 1.0, is non-increasing and flattens by its last two entries; cycle_toll_growth exceeds 1.
checks.evidence: Array [1.0, 0.434, 0.434, 0.434]: starts at 1.0, non-increasing (deltas -0.566, 0.000, 0.000), and the last two entries are identical, so the benefit saturates exactly as the measured study says it does (entry_peak_heat is 71.7 at 1, 2 and 3 skims at the top sample). cycle_toll_growth 1.17 > 1, with cycle_toll_base_pct 3.1 giving tolls 3.100/3.627/4.244/4.965 and a 25-pass feather costing 3.1*(1.17^25 - 1)/0.17 = 905.5% of plate plus 24 skim terms at 1.963 = 47.1% — unavailable, which is what bounds pass count.

checks.statement: Parachute descent speed at full hold is under the 5 m/s soft-landing threshold but above about 3.5 m/s, so the Parachute upgrade is a real purchase.
checks.evidence: Flown touchdown at full hold is 4.83 m/s from all three sample altitudes (spread_across_bands_ms 0.0), against landing.soft_landing_ms 5.0 — 3.4% of margin — and 38% above the 3.5 m/s floor. Empty lands at 3.85 and the module at 7.28. Note the flown hold is 805.5 kg; at the catalog's 1,391 kg hold the same canopy gives sqrt(2*2,791*9/(1.5*1.8*630)) = 5.43 m/s, over the line — carried to observations.

checks.statement: The claimed full-hold descent speed is what the stated canopy actually flies.
checks.evidence: parachute.independent is true — landing.parachute_area_m2 630 and parachute_drag_coefficient 1.8 are both stated in the params and were flown as stated, so this is a real measurement and not a tautology. claimed_full_hold_ms 3.99 against measured_full_hold_ms 4.83, delta_ms 0.84 = 21.1% of the claim, against a 5% tolerance (0.20 m/s). The canopy is not implicated: sqrt(2*2,205.5*9/(1.5*1.8*630)) = sqrt(23.339) = 4.83 m/s reproduces the measurement exactly, so the entire disagreement is the mass the claim was computed on — 1,504.1 kg all-up in balance_notes (a 104.1 kg hold) against 2,205.5 kg flown (an 805.5 kg hold).
checks.fix_hint: Raise landing.descent_speed_full_hold_ms to the speed the stated canopy flies at the hold mass actually loaded (4.83 m/s at 2,205.5 kg all-up) instead of deriving it from the 104.1 kg hold.

checks.statement: The tow fee is zero inside the free radius, linear beyond it, clamps at exactly 50% of haul value, and can never go negative.
checks.evidence: tow_fee.free_radius_m 1,200 (GDD's '~1,200 m'), curve 'linear', max_fee_fraction 0.50 — exactly the stated cap, not 0.45 or 0.55. Expressed as a fraction of haul value, so fee = clamp(0, (d - 1200) * slope, 0.5) * haul: zero at d <= 1,200, monotone increasing beyond, and bounded above by 0.5 * haul and below by 0. With the slope the balancer states (8.0e-7 per metre) the clamp binds at 1,200 + 0.5/8.0e-7 = 626,200 m, just inside half the planet's circumference (pi * 200,000 = 628,319 m), so the cap is reachable rather than decorative. A haul can never be worth less than nothing, so savings are untouchable.

checks.statement: Launch cost is at or below the value of three cheap pieces near the floor of the band.
checks.evidence: Value = size_class_base_value * (1 + 4.5*(h - 50,000)/230,000). Cheapest ordinary floor piece, crumpled_panel_stack at 56,000 m, small: 40 * (1 + 4.5*6,000/230,000) = 40 * 1.1174 = 44.70. Three of them = 134.1 against economy.launch_cost 120 — the launch is 2.68 cheap pieces, inside GDD 2.5's 'two to three'. Even the lightest piece in the game, torn_foil_blanket at 52,500 m, prices at 40 * 1.0489 = 41.96 before its fragile premium, and three make 125.9 > 120.

checks.statement: Steady-state towing tension at the heaviest legal two-piece load stays below magnet_hold_force_n with margin.
checks.evidence: Heaviest hand-tetherable ordinary piece is impact_pitted_engine_bell at 523 kg; eva.base_tether_slots 2, so the worst legal load is 1,046 kg. a = jetpack_thrust_n / (suit_mass_kg + towed) = 240 / (110 + 1,046) = 0.2076 m/s^2, per-cable tension = 523 * 0.2076 = 108.6 N against magnet_hold_force_n 900 — an 8.3x margin. The bound is structural: steady tension can never exceed jetpack thrust itself (240 N), so even Armstrong's module at 3,600 kg gives 240/(110+3,600) = 0.0647 m/s^2 and 232.9 N, still 3.9x under the hold force. Shear cannot fire during normal flying.

checks.statement: No parameter anywhere reintroduces thrust after staging.
checks.evidence: The params contain exactly three thrust quantities: flight.thrust_n 57,000 and flight.rcs_thrust_n 2,600 (both on the jettisoned thruster/tank stack) and eva.jetpack_thrust_n 240 (on the astronaut, not the ship). There is no post-stage, reserve, retro or landing-thrust key, and no upgrade entry names one — the twelve purchases affect magnet_range_screens, fuel_capacity_kg, thrust_n, parachute_area_m2, base_slots and heat_capacity only. Nothing restores propulsion to a staged ship.

checks.statement: Fragile pieces are never crushable at any compactor tier present in the params, and the fragile premium makes one intact fragile piece worth several solid pieces of the same class nearby.
checks.evidence: cargo.compactor_tier is 1, the only tier present. All twelve fragile pieces carry crushable false: torn_foil_blanket, cracked_solar_array, shredded_antenna_mesh, delaminated_radiator_fin, cracked_optics_barrel, shattered_star_tracker, cracked_ablative_nose_cone, split_avionics_rack, cracked_deep_space_dish, fused_ion_grid_assembly, shattered_cryo_dewar, cracked_command_module_hatch. No piece in the catalog has fragile true and crushable true. Premium: economy.fragile_value_premium 3, so cracked_optics_barrel (small, 138,000 m) prices at 40 * (1 + 4.5*88,000/230,000) * 3 = 40 * 2.722 * 3 = 326.6 against dead_thruster_quad (small, solid, 152,500 m) at 40 * 3.005 = 120.2 — 2.7 solid pieces of the same class from higher up, and 3.0x against a solid small at the same altitude.

checks.statement: Oversized junk rejects the hand magnet.
checks.evidence: size_classes.oversized.hand_tetherable is false (small and medium are true), and shipping_slice.oversized_reachable is false. The three oversized pieces — collapsed_dish_frame (86,500 m, 445 kg), buckled_pressure_bulkhead (160,000 m, 686 kg), severed_boom_mast (234,000 m, 828 kg) — are therefore visible and unliftable, and the player meets the refusal at 86,500 m, inside the shipping slice.

checks.statement: Twelve purchases: six parts, two tiers each, tier 2 dearer than tier 1, and each tier improving the stat it names.
checks.evidence: 12 entries over exactly six parts. Costs, tier 1 -> tier 2, all strictly increasing: hand_magnet 680 -> 1,500; fuel_tank 750 -> 1,600; thruster 850 -> 1,900; parachute 1,000 -> 2,350; storage 1,100 -> 2,500; heat_shield 1,250 -> 2,950; total 18,430. Each stat improves monotonically from its base: magnet_range_screens 0.125 -> 0.1875 -> 0.25; fuel_capacity_kg 860 -> 1,250 -> 1,600; thrust_n 57,000 -> 66,000 -> 76,000; parachute_area_m2 630 -> 900 -> 1,400; base_slots 6 -> 9 -> 12; heat_capacity 185 -> 215 -> 245. Every part ships at a starter value and is bought up twice, as GDD 2.5 requires.

checks.statement: The climb's peak heat stays under reentry.heat_capacity.
checks.evidence: climb_peak_heat is 37.5 on the bottom-sample route and 36.0 on the middle-sample route, both with climb_survivable true; the top-sample row logs 0 because that ascent never got airborne to the band (see shipping_slice_reachable). Hottest measured climb = 37.5 against reentry.heat_capacity 185 — 20.3% of the bar, 79.7% of margin. The ascent's exemption from the 3x unstaged penalty is doing exactly what GDD 2.2 asks: the first flight cannot burn up.

checks.statement: The base ship reaches the band floor and the shipping slice is populated with fragility and at least two size classes in both of its thirds.
checks.evidence: Route is 'arc', not orbit, and that is legal: the bottom sample at 65,000 m — 15,000 m above the 50,000 m floor — is reached with arc_apex_m 73,875, arc_eva_window_s 125.9 and arc_fuel_margin_pct 13.3 (fuel_remaining_kg 130.51 of 860). The middle sample at 115,000 m is also reached on an arc, apex 131,482 m, window 203.2 s, margin 5.1%. Both fail to circularise ('out of fuel before circularising'), which is the GDD 2.5 progression beat rather than a reachability failure, and 125.9 s settles GDD 4.5's open 97 s question upward. Catalog population — bottom third (50,000-126,667 m): 11 pieces, size classes small/medium/oversized, fragile present (torn_foil_blanket 52,500, cracked_solar_array 61,500, shredded_antenna_mesh 93,000, delaminated_radiator_fin 120,000). Middle third (126,667-203,333 m): 10 pieces, small/medium/oversized, fragile present (cracked_optics_barrel 138,000, shattered_star_tracker 174,000, cracked_ablative_nose_cone 189,000, split_avionics_rack 197,500). Both thirds meet crushing and fragility.

checks.statement: No rule passes only because a quantity the design document fixes in prose was widened to meet it.
checks.evidence: Every GDD-stated constant is at its stated value: cargo.base_slots 6 ('Cargo reads 4 of 6'), eva.base_tether_slots 2, eva.magnet_range_screens 0.125 (~1/8 screen), reentry.commit_floor_m 8,000, reentry.unstaged_heat_multiplier 3, reentry.heat_dissipation_s 5, reentry.cargo_damage_interval_s 3, landing.soft_landing_ms 5, landing.no_gear_multiplier 2, landing.parachute_area_m2 630 at Cd 1.8, tow_fee.free_radius_m 1,200 and max_fee_fraction 0.5, economy.value_gradient 1.0 -> 5.5, band 50,000-280,000, module mass 3,600 kg, twelve purchases over six parts. The one deviation is heat_capacity's ceiling, 245 against GDD 2.2's '~235', and the GDD marks that figure '(to set)' — it is unset by construction, not moved to pass a check, and it still respects the binding rule that no tier reaches the module's plunge peak (245 < 265.3). Independent corroboration that dry_mass_kg 1,400 was not tuned to fit: the flown top-of-band empty plunge is 144.7, identical to GDD 2.2's own stated 144.7.

observations: The harness's hold is 42% lighter than the catalog's own: cargo.kg_per_slot 134.25 and full_hold_kg 805.5, against 231.89 kg/slot spawn-weighted over the hand-tetherable shipping slice and 1,391 kg for six slots — which is the number GDD 2.2 flew at ~1,398 kg. Every full-hold figure in this sweep is therefore optimistic, and two passing checks are sensitive to it. Extrapolating the flown mass-to-peak curve (144.7 at 1,400 kg all-up, 180.1 at 2,205.5, exponent 0.49) puts the catalog's full hold at roughly 204 bar units on a top-of-band plunge — above heat_capacity 185 and above the module's best skimmed descent of 188.9, which would invert the third leg of heavy_descent_requires_multi_pass. The same canopy at 2,791 kg all-up gives sqrt(2*2,791*9/1,701) = 5.43 m/s, over the 5.0 soft line. Nothing in either agent's artifact can reconcile this; it is the hold model in the harness that needs to agree with shipping_slice.slots_per_piece before the next sweep is trusted.

The base capacity's margin over the loads it must let plunge is 2-3%, not the 32% GDD 2.2 says it is building on. From the top of the band, full hold 180.1 and the heaviest single ordinary piece (828 kg) 181.0 against heat_capacity 185. GDD 2.2 explicitly rejects a 4%-wide window as 'a coincidence and not a mechanic'; this is of that order, and it is where the hold-mass disagreement above lands first.

cost_curve's bottom and middle rows are priced off the top sample's skim multiplier. The flight measured 0.700 at the bottom and 0.528 at the middle, not 0.434. On the bottom's own value the one-skim entry term is 0.0009*70^2 = 4.410 and the one-skim cost is 6.727 + 4.410 + 1.963 = 13.10 against a 12.10 plunge, so the bottom's true argmin is 0, not the 1 the array reports. The Balancer says this plainly and cannot fix it — the schema holds one array where the physics needs three. A per-sample skim_heat_multiplier is the change, and it is a schema change, not a value change.

The module lands hard on every canopy that was flown. Touchdown is 7.28 m/s from all three sample altitudes on the base 630 m^2 canopy — 46% over the soft line, graded soft_landing false — and the sweep flies a perfect pilot with no flare error. So a competently flown finale loses one module state on touchdown regardless of heat, and pristine is unreachable without parachute tier 2 (1,400 m^2, predicted 4.88 m/s, never flown). That makes the parachute track, not the shield track, the gate on the triumph ending, which GDD 2.6 does not say anywhere.

Ordinary cargo never lands hard, so two thirds of the hold-mass scale has nothing to show. Touchdown moves 3.85 (empty) -> 4.37 (half) -> 4.83 (full) -> 4.86 (heaviest ordinary piece), a 1.01 m/s spread that never crosses 5.0. GDD 2.4's dial is painted green/amber/red; at this canopy and this hold model everything a player can actually haul is green. Greed is paid for in plate (7.6% -> 10.4% at the bottom) and in heat (70 -> 90), not in landings.

The starter shield's first lesson is a fifth of the bar, where GDD 4.4 wanted about half. The climb peaks at 37.5 against heat_capacity 185 — 20.3%. The obvious fix is blocked: 185 is pinned between the full hold's 180.1 plunge and the module's gate, so it cannot be lowered to sharpen the lesson. If the first launch is meant to look alarming, the lever has to be the climb's heat, not the bar's capacity.

The top of the band was never actually flown. The base ship 'crashed on ascent' with an arc apex of 192,203 m against a 215,000 m sample — 10.6% short — so every top-of-band descent in this sweep was flown from an altitude the flown configuration cannot reach, and no upgraded ship (tank, shield or parachute tier) was flown at all. The Balancer's claim that fuel_tank tier 2 circularises at the top with 9% left is untested, and GDD section 3's questions 6 and 8 — module infeasible-as-plunge at every shield tier, module run beatable at full upgrades — remain unmeasured.

The module's plunge ban is a property of its altitude as much as its mass. From the bottom of the band the 3,600 kg load plunges at 177.7, under the 185 bar; from the middle it is 212.7 and from the top 265.3. The rule holds where it must because the module hangs at 277,000 m, but if anything ever moves it down the envelope, the endgame's gate quietly opens.

ablation.skim_peak 46.7 charges 0.0009*46.7^2 = 1.96% of plate per skim — about 12% of a one-skim descent's cost at the bottom — and the flight reports skim_peak_heat as 0.0 in every row of every skim study at all three samples. Either skims deposit no bar heat in this model or the field is unpopulated; on both readings the constant is unsupported by anything measured.
